name: Privacy Impact Assessment
description: Map personal-data flows, purposes, actors, risks, controls, retention, user rights, and residual privacy risk before or during product deployment.

tasks.name: Define system and privacy context
tasks.objective: Define product/process, people affected, jurisdictions/policies, business purpose, decision owners, lifecycle stage, and material changes triggering assessment.

tasks.name: Map data lifecycle
tasks.objective: Inventory personal and sensitive data, sources, collection context, inferred data, identifiers, storage, transfers, processors, recipients, automated decisions, retention, deletion, and cross-border flows.

tasks.name: Test purpose and necessity
tasks.objective: For each data element and flow, identify purpose, necessity/proportionality, user expectation, alternatives with less data, secondary-use risk, and whether data minimization can eliminate the exposure.

tasks.name: Analyze privacy risk
tasks.objective: Identify risks to individuals from surveillance, exposure, reidentification, discrimination, manipulation, chilling effects, loss of autonomy, inappropriate inference, retention, access abuse, and inaccurate data; model likelihood and impact with affected populations in view.

tasks.name: Design controls
tasks.objective: Apply minimization, separation, access control, encryption, privacy-preserving computation, retention/deletion, consent or preference handling, transparency, rights workflows, audit, vendor clauses, testing, and incident response at the earliest effective point.

tasks.name: Assess residual risk and approvals
tasks.objective: Re-score risk after controls, document accepted residual risk, unresolved legal/policy questions for qualified review, control owners, launch blockers, and re-assessment triggers.

tasks.name: Publish living assessment
tasks.objective: Produce the data-flow map, purpose table, risk register, mitigations, residual-risk decisions, retention schedule, vendor dependencies, rights/incident procedures, and change triggers. Avoid pretending the assessment is legal advice.
